mind_map.root_node: Far and Near (Metric Length Units, Conversions & Double Number Lines)

key_nodes: Millimetre (mm): Micro unit for tiny object dimensions and thickness (e.g., coin thickness, eraser edge)
Centimetre (cm): Unit for small handheld items (e.g., pencil length, notebook width; 1 cm = 10 mm)
Metre (m): Base metric unit for human height, room dimensions, fabric cuts (1 m = 100 cm = 1,000 mm)
Kilometre (km): Macro unit for geographical distances between towns and cities (1 km = 1,000 m)
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Confusing mm and cm markers on standard ruler scales (cm marks are numbered; mm marks are unnumbered sub-lines).
sub_branches.formula_or_rule: Metric Equivalences: 1 cm = 10 mm; 1 m = 100 cm; 1 km = 1,000 m.
sub_branches.real_world_application: Selecting appropriate tools (ruler vs tape measure) for tailoring or construction.

sub_branches.sub_title: Micro to Macro Orders of Magnitude
key_nodes: Relative Scaling: 1 km = 1,000 m = 100,000 cm = 1,000,000 mm
Contextual Selection: Choosing mm for seeds, cm for shoes, m for sprinting tracks, km for flight paths
Precision Trade-offs: Small units increase precision; large units simplify geographical tracking
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Using metres to measure road trip distances between cities (leads to unnecessarily large numbers).
sub_branches.formula_or_rule: Unit Choice Rule: Select the unit whose magnitude matches the object being measured.
sub_branches.real_world_application: Engineering design specifications and geographical atlas mapping.

key_nodes: Larger to Smaller Unit: Multiply by conversion scale factor (e.g., 3.5 km x 1,000 = 3,500 m)
Smaller to Larger Unit: Divide by conversion factor (e.g., 450 cm / 100 = 4.5 m)
Compound Conversion: Expressing fractional lengths (e.g., 2 m 45 cm = 245 cm)
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Multiplying instead of dividing when converting smaller metric units to larger metric units.
sub_branches.formula_or_rule: Conversion Rule: Large -> Small (Multiply by factor); Small -> Large (Divide by factor).
sub_branches.real_world_application: Converting architectural blueprints to actual building site measurements.

key_nodes: Double Number Line Structure: Two parallel aligned axes showing equivalent values in different units
Proportional Visualization: Mapping fractional intervals (e.g., top axis in metres: 0, 0.5, 1; bottom axis in cm: 0, 50, 100)
Interpolation of Intermediate Values: Finding non-standard unit matches visually
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Misaligning zero origins or maintaining unequal tick spacing on top and bottom number lines.
sub_branches.formula_or_rule: Proportional Mapping: Aligned vertical ticks on double number lines represent equal physical lengths.
sub_branches.real_world_application: Dual metric-imperial tape measures and athletic track marking.

key_nodes: Column Addition of Lengths: Adding m and cm separately; regrouping 100 cm as 1 m
Column Subtraction of Lengths: Borrowing 1 m as 100 cm when cm minuend < cm subtrahend
Multi-leg Total Calculation: Summing route segments to determine marathon lengths
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Borrowing 10 cm instead of 100 cm when regrouping metres to centimetres.
sub_branches.formula_or_rule: Length Regrouping: 100 cm = 1 m; 1,000 m = 1 km.
sub_branches.real_world_application: Tailoring fabric cuts and road construction survey logs.

key_nodes: Map Scale Ratio: Proportional reduction scaling ground distances onto printable paper (e.g., 1 cm on map = 10 km on ground)
Ground Distance Calculation: Ground Distance = Map Distance (cm) x Scale Factor (km/cm)
Map Distance Calculation: Map Distance = Ground Distance / Scale Factor
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Treating map scale as direct 1:1 physical distance without multiplying by ground factor.
sub_branches.formula_or_rule: Ground Distance = Measured Map Centimetres x Kilometres per Map Centimetre.
sub_branches.real_world_application: Navigating highway road maps, hiking trails, and urban city planning blueprints.
